newsitem.title: UK: 600 Group tumbles after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: 600 Group tumbles after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in machine tool maker The 600 Group Plc plummeted on Tuesday after the company warned that profits in the current financial year were unlikely to meet market expectations.
The stock was down 51p at 148-1/2 by 0835 GMT.
In a trading statement, the company said the weakness in UK demand for machine tools, which it originally reported last summer, had continued through the last quarter of 1996.

It said the effects of this were compounded by the high level of stocks held by UK dealers of computer-controlled machine tools, built up in anticipation of the normal increase in activity in the second half.
"The overall impact of these developments...is that profits in the current financial year should show an improvement over last year but are unlikely to meet current market expectations," it said.
However it said new initiatives in the U.S. on computer-controlled machine tools were generating higher sales while world sales of the Alpha electronic lathe continued to set new records.
Today's decline in the stock to 147p at one stage took it back to its lowest since October 1995.
Last April the company said it expected profits for 1996 to be about 9.5 million stg, well above the then market consensus of some 7.9 million stg.
